rows.query: Master circular for ESG rating providers
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular for ESG Rating Providers ("ERPs") is a document that provides regulatory guidelines for ESG Rating Providers. It is issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and is effective from July 4, 2023. The circular specifies the registration, general obligations, manner of inspection, and code of conduct for ERPs. It also provides procedural and disclosure requirements for ERPs, enabling the industry and other users to have access to all applicable directions to ERPs at one place. ERPs are directed to comply with the conditions laid down in this master circular and have necessary systems and infrastructure in place for implementation. The circular also specifies the disclosure of rating rationale on the website of ERPs.

rows.query: Master circular for debenture trustees
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular for Debenture Trustees (DTs) has been prepared by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to provide users with access to all applicable circulars/directions at one place. This circular is a compilation of the circulars/communications issued by SEBI up to March 31, 2018. It is effective from the date of its issue. In case of any inconsistency between the Master Circular and the applicable circulars, the contents of the relevant circular shall prevail. The Master Circular is a compilation of all the existing/ applicable circulars issued by the Market Intermediaries Regulation and Supervision Department of SEBI to Debenture Trustees. Efforts have been made to incorporate applicable provisions of existing circulars issued by other Departments of SEBI relevant to Debenture Trustees.

rows.query: Master circular on the framework for the Social Stock Exchange
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular on the Framework for the Social Stock Exchange (SSE) is a document issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). It consolidates circulars/directions issued by SEBI up to March 31, 2014. This circular is designed to provide users with an access to all the applicable circulars/directions at one place. rows.query: Review of the block deal framework
rows.answer_text: The block deal framework has been reviewed and modified based on the Working Group's recommendations, the deliberations of the Secondary Market Advisory Committee (SMAC), and public comments. The new framework requires certain changes to be made in the systems and processes of clearing corporations, stock exchanges, depositories, stock brokers, and NPCI. The Stock Exchanges are permitted to provide a separate trading window during the morning session from 08:45 AM to 09:00 AM, in addition to the existing Block Deal windows from 08:45 AM to 09:00 AM and 2:05 PM to 2:20 PM for T+1 settlement cycle. The Block Deal window under the optional T+0 settlement cycle shall be available only for the morning session from 08:45 AM to 09:00 AM. Trades in the optional T+0 block window session will be settled on T+0 settlement cycle.

rows.query: Revision of the order-to-trade ratio framework
rows.answer_text: The order-to-trade ratio (OTR) framework has been revised to prescribe effective economic disincentives by Stock Exchanges for high OTR of Algorithmic orders placed by Trading Members (TMs). This framework includes penalties for higher OTR, a cooling-off period for algorithmic trading, and the exclusion of algorithmic orders within 1% of the last traded price (LTP) from the calculation of OTR. The penalty structure is applicable to members placing more than 10,000 orders in a day. Monitoring systems are put in place to identify and impede any possible instances of order flooding by algorithmic trading.

rows.query: Format of the disclosure document for portfolio managers
rows.answer_text:
The format of the disclosure document for portfolio managers is as follows:

1. **History, Present Business, and Background of the Portfolio Manager**
2. **Promoters, Directors, and Their Background**
3. **Top 10 Group Companies/Firms of the Portfolio Manager on Turnover Basis**
4. **Details of the Services Being Offered: Discretionary/Non-discretionary/Advisory**

For investment details, the disclosure document should include:

1. **Investments in the Securities of Associates/Related Parties of the Portfolio Manager**
   - **Sr.** - Name of Investment
   - **Name of Investment** - Name of Investment
   - **Amount** - Amount
   - **Cost of Investment** - Cost of Investment
   - **Value of Investment** - Value of Investment
   - **Percentage of Total AUM** - Percentage of Total AUM

rows.query: Reclassification of REITs as equity related instruments
rows.answer_text: With a view to facilitate enhanced participation by Mutual Funds and Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs), the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, to reclassify Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as equity-related instruments. This reclassification is aimed at enhancing the participation of Mutual Funds and SIFs in the investment of their funds in REITs. The reclassification will take effect from January 1, 2026, with any investment made by Mutual Funds and SIFs in REITs considered as investment in equity-related instruments. Existing investments in REITs held by debt schemes of Mutual Funds and investment strategies of SIFs as on December 31, 2025, shall be grandfathered, but AMCs are encouraged to divest REITs from respective portfolios of debt schemes considering the market conditions, liquidity, and interest of investors

rows.query: Creation and invocation of pledge of securities through the depository system
rows.answer_text:
The creation and invocation of a pledge of securities through the depository system are governed by specific rules and procedures. According to the Circular HO/47/14/12(1)2026-MRD-POD2/I/4229/2026, the operational mechanism for margin pledge involves the following steps:

1. **Creation of Pledge**: When a client's securities are pledged with a Depository, the securities are transferred to the Demat account of the Depository.

2. **Invocation of Pledge**: If a client's securities are re-pledged with another Depository, the Depository must ensure that the pay-in of securities is done on the same day of invocation.

3. **Margin Obligation**: The Circular specifies that the obligation to provide securities for margin purposes is given by the Depository to the TM/CM, as the case may be.

4. **Off-market Transfer**: Any procedure not following the specified provisions

rows.query: Norms for sharing and usage of stock exchange price data for educational purposes
rows.answer_text:
The norms for sharing and usage of stock exchange price data for educational purposes are as follows:

- A time lag of 30 days is prescribed for both sharing and usage of price data for educational purposes.

- The data shared for educational purposes shall be segregated into two baskets:

  1. For research/research publications undertaken by accredited academic institutions, the data shall be shared with a lag of 1 day.

  2. For other purposes, the data shall be shared without offering any kind of monetary incentive to the participants.

- The legal agreement for sharing the data shall have provisions to prevent any kind of misuse by the entities.

- The MIIs and market intermediaries are advised to ensure due diligence while sharing such data.

- The MIIs and market intermediaries are advised to take necessary steps to avoid misuse of price data by entities with whom the data is being shared.

- The data shared with vendors for commercial purposes shall not fall under this policy.

rows.query: How old must exchange quotes be before a teaching institute that is not a regulated entity can show them to students?
rows.answer_text: The Circular dated May 24, 2024 allowed exchanges to share data for educational purposes with a time lag of one day. The Circular dated January 29, 2025 operates after that as to how much old data can be actually used for sole educational purposes and for that a time lag of three months had been prescribed. Therefore, before a teaching institute that is not a regulated entity can show old exchange data to students, the data must be at least three months old.

rows.query: Can an asset manager take a short-term bank loan to bridge a same-day cash mismatch when paying out exiting unitholders?
rows.answer_text: Yes, an asset manager can take a short-term bank loan to bridge a same-day cash mismatch when paying out exiting unitholders. This is permitted under the Master Circular for Mutual Funds, as per clause 12.16.1.3, which states that no mutual fund scheme shall park more than 15% of their net assets in short-term deposits of all scheduled commercial banks together. This limit may be raised to 20% with prior approval from the Trustees.

rows.query: Can an investor voluntarily block all outgoing transactions from their folio until they choose to re-enable them?
rows.answer_text: Yes, an investor can voluntarily block all outgoing transactions from their folio until they choose to re-enable them. This is facilitated by the Voluntary Lock-in/Debit Freeze facility, which is introduced by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in the first phase of the process. This facility is made available to mutual fund investors through the Mutual Fund Central Platform, where the RTAs (Registration Transfer Agents) provide the facility to lock the folio. This process is laid down in the Circular dated June 23, 2023, under the Master Circular for Depositories, which outlines the general features of the framework for Trading Members to provide the facility of voluntary freezing/blocking the online access of the trading account to their clients on account of suspicious activities. This facility is introduced as a non-mandatory option to be provided by the stock broker, allowing investors to choose to avail UPI block facility under some broker(s) and non-UPI based trading under others.

rows.query: How will the day's final stock price be determined instead of the volume-weighted average of the last half hour of trading?
rows.answer_text: The final stock price will be determined by the underlying index price arrived at based on Volume Weightage Average Price of the constituents of the underlying index between 4:00 pm and 5:00 pm on the expiry day of the Index options contract. If there is no trading in any constituent during the last one hour, the stock exchange will determine an appropriate methodology to arrive at the appropriate price of the constituent to be used for determining the index price.

rows.query: What net and gross futures-equivalent exposure caps apply to index options during the trading day, and how are they monitored?
rows.answer_text:
The net and gross futures-equivalent exposure caps for index options during the trading day are as follows:

- **End of Day**: ₹500 crores net, ₹1,500 crores gross
- **Intraday**: ₹1,000 crores net, ₹2,500 crores gross

These caps are monitored by Stock Exchanges/CCs. If the net or gross futures-equivalent exposure exceeds these limits, the Stock Exchanges/CCs are required to intimate the entities (and their TM/CM) within 9 PM on each trading day.

rows.query: What new requirements govern the appointment and duties of the MD, CTO and CISO at exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories?
rows.answer_text: The new requirements stipulate that the Key Management Personnel (KMPs) of MIIs in crucial areas such as compliance, risk management, technology, and information security must be of appropriate stature and independence. These KMPs include the Compliance Officer, Chief Risk Officer, Chief Technology Officer, and Chief Information Security Officer. The MIIs are required to insert a clause in the terms of appointment of these officials and/or in the Internal Code of Conduct to comply with the "financial disincentive" requirements. The MD and CTO are not explicitly mentioned as KMPs, but the MD is included in the Standing Committee on Technology. The CTO and CISO are invited to meetings of the Committee, and the committee shall be chaired by the PID with expertise in technology.

rows.query: What is the tender offer route procedure and timeline for a listed company repurchasing its own shares?
rows.answer_text:

1. **Filing of Public Announcement**: The listed company files a public announcement on the SEBI website within 2 working days from the Board meeting date.

2. **Filing of Detailed Public Statement**: The detailed public statement is filed within 5 working days of the filing of the public announcement.

3. **Dispatch of Letter of Offer**: The letter of offer is dispatched within 7 working days of receiving the observation letter from SEBI.

4. **Publication of Independent Director's Recommendation**: The independent director's recommendation is published 2 working days prior to the commencement of the tendering period.

5. **Offer Opening**: The offer opens not later than 12 working days from the date of receipt of the observation letter from SEBI.

6. **Availability of Letter of Offer**: The letter of offer is available till the offer closure date.

rows.query: What disclosures must a listed company make for employee stock option schemes under the share based employee benefits framework?
rows.answer_text:
A listed company must comply with the following requirements for disclosure of Employee Benefit Scheme Documents in terms of Regulation 46(2)(za) of the LODR:

a. The scheme document shall be uploaded on the website of the listed entity after obtaining shareholder approval as required under SEBI (SBEB) Regulations, 2021.

b. The documents uploaded on the website shall mandatorily have minimum information to be disclosed to shareholders as per SEBI (SBEB) Regulations, 2021.

c. The rationale for redacting information from the documents and the justification as to how such redacted information would affect competitive position or reveal commercial secrets of the listed entity shall be placed before the board of directors for consideration and approval.

The secretarial compliance report issued by a Peer Reviewed Company Secretary under Regulation 24A(2) of the LODR Regulations shall include a confirmation on compliance with the aforesaid requirements by the listed entity.

rows.query: What is the framework for trading electronic gold receipts on stock exchanges?
rows.answer_text:
The framework for trading electronic gold receipts (EGR) on stock exchanges in India is as follows:

- **Tranches**: The entire transaction in the EGR segment is divided into three tranches.
- **Tranche 1**: Physical gold is converted into EGR.
- **Tranche 2**: EGR is traded on stock exchanges.
- **Tranche 3**: EGR can be converted into physical gold.

- **Stock exchanges may launch contracts with different denominations for trading and/or conversion of EGR into gold.

- **Approval**: Stock exchanges desirous of trading in EGRs may apply to SEBI for approval of trading of EGRs in the new segment.

rows.query: What are the registration requirements for foreign venture capital investors?
rows.answer_text: The registration requirements for foreign venture capital investors (FVCIs) include obtaining a firm commitment from their investors for a contribution of at least USD 1 million at the time of application. This commitment must be obtained from investors who are resident in the country of the FVCI. The FVCI must also comply with the conditions specified in the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008, which include not engaging in any transaction in the account of the FVCI, and the DDP (Designated Depository Participant) must notify such instances to SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) within seven days. The DDP is responsible for monitoring compliance of the FVCI with the conditions specified. The FVCI must also comply with the operational instructions/directives issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India.

rows.query: How is the Investor Protection and Education Fund utilised and administered?
rows.answer_text: The Investor Protection and Education Fund (IPF) is administered by a Trust created for this purpose. The IPF Trust of the stock exchange shall have maximum 5 trustees. The IPF Trust shall consist of three public interest directors, one representative from investor associations recognized by SEBI, and the compliance officer of the stock exchange. The maximum tenure of a trustee (excluding the compliance officer of the exchange, whose trusteeship would be co-terminus with the service) shall be five years or as specified by SEBI. The IPF Trust shall be responsible for the administration of the IPF, ensuring its effective utilization, and maintaining the funds in a separate account from the Stock Exchange's funds. The funds in the IPF are well segregated from those of the Stock Exchange, and the IPF is immune from any liability of the exchange. The IPF shall be utilized for purposes of investor/client education, awareness, research, or other such programmes as may be decided by SEBI.

rows.query: What are a credit rating agency's obligations under SEBI's 2026 circular when it rates an instrument that another financial sector regulator also oversees?
rows.answer_text:
A credit rating agency's obligations under SEBI's 2026 circular when it rates an instrument that another financial sector regulator also oversees are as follows:

- The agency must abide by the rules/regulations/directions/guidelines applicable to or governing the instrument/products/securities as prescribed by the financial sector regulator.

- If the instrument is listed on a Recognized Stock Exchange, the Board's rules/regulations/directions specified by the Board shall continue to be applicable.

- The agency's ratings under the guidelines of the International Financial Services Centre Authority (IFSCA) are under the purview of IFSCA.

- The circular specifies that any issues arising from the activities of SEBI registered CRAs in the International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) shall be dealt with by IFSCA under the IFSCA's guidelines.

- The agency must ensure that the information provided to the Depository Transfer (DT) on the specified submission platform is sent by the CRA to the DT

rows.query: What do SEBI's 2019 guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism require of securities market intermediaries?
rows.answer_text: According to the 2019 guidelines on Anti-Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism issued by SEBI, securities market intermediaries are required to establish policies and procedures to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing. The guidelines advise each registered intermediary to consider the specific nature of its business, organizational structure, type of clients, and transactions when implementing the suggested measures and procedures. The guidelines also state that the overriding principle is that the measures taken by the intermediary should be adequate, appropriate, and abide by the spirit of the measures and the requirements as enshrined in the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and Rules framed thereunder.

rows.answer_text:

rows.query: Can a custodian share staff and IT systems with its other financial businesses, and what conflict-of-interest rules still apply?
rows.answer_text: Yes, a custodian can share staff and IT systems with its other financial businesses. However, the custodian must adhere to general guidelines specified by SEBI, as outlined in the Circular no. CIR/MIRSD/5/2013 dated August 27, 2013. These guidelines include adherence to general guidelines, adherence to SEBI Circular no. CIR/MIRSD/5/2013, and the requirement to file an annual review report with SEBI. The custodian must also comply with Regulation 13 of the Custodian Regulations, which stipulates that the custodian's systems, procedures, and controls must be reviewed by an expert annually. The custodian must file the review report by March 31st of the following year. Additionally, the custodian must comply with Regulation 25 of the FPI Regulations, which requires the custodian to report FPI transactions to SEBI and RBI.

rows.query: After a company's share transfer agent finishes processing a share transfer, how and when do they need to tell the depository participant about it?
rows.answer_text: After a company's share transfer agent finishes processing a share transfer, they need to tell the depository participant about it by intimating the depository about the lock-in and its period. This information must be provided within one year from the date of the transfer. If a fraud is detected during this period, the lock-in shall continue on the related securities until further intimation. In such cases, securities so locked-in shall be released only in favour of the claimant as per order from the competent court for the release of securities.

rows.answer_text: The approval for a transaction of sale or purchase of a security by the access person shall not be valid for more than 7 trading days from the date of approval. rows.query: Are stockbrokers required to keep their clients' money in a separate bank account from their own funds?
rows.answer_text: Yes, stockbrokers are required to keep their clients' money in a separate bank account from their own funds. This is a fundamental requirement under the Master Circular for Stock Brokers, as well as other relevant circulars, notices, guidelines, and regulations issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The circulars emphasize the importance of maintaining the integrity of the brokerage system by ensuring that clients' funds are kept separate from the broker's own funds. This practice helps in maintaining the trust of clients and adheres to the regulatory standards set by SEBI.

rows.query: If a broker's employee receives some market news or rumor by email, do they need approval before forwarding it to others?
rows.answer_text: Yes, according to the circulars retrieved, if a broker's employee receives any market-related news or rumor by email, they should forward it only after the same has been seen and approved by the concerned Intermediary's Compliance Officer. If an employee fails to do so, they are deemed to have violated the various provisions contained in SEBI Act and the Rules/Regulations framed thereunder, and shall be liable for action. The Compliance Officer shall also be held liable for breach of duty in this regard.

rows.query: Are regulated entities required to keep backup 'template' copies of their critical IT systems at a separate location, in case they need to rebuild in an emergency?
rows.answer_text: Yes, regulated entities are required to maintain regularly updated 'golden images' of their critical IT systems at offsite locations. This entails maintaining image "templates" that include a preconfigured operating system (OS) and associated software applications that can be quickly deployed to rebuild a system, such as a virtual machine or server. This practice is aimed at ensuring the availability of critical systems in the event of a disaster or emergency.

rows.query: How does a mutual fund investor find out if they have unclaimed money sitting with a fund, and what proof of identity do they need?
rows.answer_text: A mutual fund investor can find out if they have unclaimed money by checking the list of names and addresses of investors in whose folios there are unclaimed amounts on the mutual fund's website. To obtain this information, the investor must provide their appropriate credentials (like PAN, date of birth, etc.) along with adequate security control measures being put in place by the Mutual Fund / AMFI. The investor can also obtain information on the process of claiming the unclaimed amount and the necessary forms / documents required for the same on the mutual fund's website. Additionally, the investor can obtain information on the prevailing value of the unclaimed amount by the periodic statement of accounts / Consolidated Account Statement sent to the investor.

rows.query: SEBI made it easier to get 'accredited investor' status recently — what changed to simplify the process?
rows.answer_text:
The process to simplify the grant of accreditation to investors, including 'accredited investors', was simplified by SEBI. This was done by issuing the following circular:

**Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD1/CIR/2023/189 dated December 18, 2023**  
**"Simplification of requirements for grant of accreditation to investors"**

This circular simplified the requirements for granting accreditation to investors, providing flexibility and facilitating the accreditation process.

rows.query: If the same outsourcing vendor handles work for several different brokers, what precautions are supposed to stop client data from getting mixed up between them?
rows.answer_text:
If the same outsourcing vendor handles work for several different brokers, the following precautions are supposed to stop client data from getting mixed up between them:

- Ensure that the employees of the third party have limited access to the data handled and only on a "need to know" basis
- The third party should have adequate checks and balances to ensure the same
- The intermediary and the RTA should ensure that strong safeguards are put in place so that there is no co-mingling of information /documents, records and assets.

rows.query: If a foreign bank wants to register as a Foreign Portfolio Investor in India, what makes it count as being 'appropriately regulated' back home?
rows.answer_text: If a foreign bank wants to register as a Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) in India, it would be considered 'appropriately regulated' if it is regulated by the unified financial sector regulator in its home jurisdiction or by a banking sector regulator in its home jurisdiction. This means the bank's home regulator must be one of the following: the unified financial sector regulator, or a banking sector regulator. Additionally, if the home country's central bank is not a member of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), the FPI can seek registration under Category II.

rows.query: Can a fund manager place direct market access trades on behalf of an institutional client instead of the client trading themselves?
rows.answer_text: Yes, a fund manager can place direct market access trades on behalf of an institutional client instead of the client trading themselves. This is permitted under the terms of the Master Circular for Stock Brokers, which states that a SEBI registered entity may act as an investment manager on behalf of institutional clients. In case the facility of Direct Market Access (DMA) is used by the client through an investment manager, the investment manager may execute the necessary documents on behalf of the client(s).

rows.query: If a foreign investor's trading data is stored in the cloud, does it still need to physically stay within India's legal boundaries?
rows.answer_text: No, if a foreign investor's trading data is stored in the cloud, it does not need to physically stay within India's legal boundaries. The circular states that the REs are responsible for ensuring compliance with laws, rules, regulations, etc. issued by SEBI/ Government of India/ respective state government, which includes compliance with laws related to data protection and cybersecurity. Therefore, the data can be stored outside India's legal boundaries as long as it complies with the relevant laws.

rows.query: Can a mutual fund carve out a 'segregated portfolio' just because a bond issuer looks likely to default, or does an actual default have to happen first?
rows.answer_text: Yes, an actual default has to happen first. According to the circular, the AMC may create a segregated portfolio of debt and money market instruments only if the issuer of the instrument has defaulted on either the interest or principal amount. The circular also mentions that the actual default by the issuer of such instruments shall be considered as a credit event for the creation of the segregated portfolio.

rows.query: What happens to money that REIT unitholders never claim — does it eventually go to an investor protection fund, and can they still get it back later?
rows.answer_text: Yes, the unclaimed amounts of a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) unitholders eventually go to an investor protection fund. Specifically, under Regulation 18(16)(f) of the REIT Regulations, any unclaimed or unpaid amounts declared by a REIT in terms of sub-clause (c) are transferred to the 'Investor Protection and Education Fund' constituted by the Board. This fund is then utilized for refund to the entities which transferred the said amounts, pursuant to their making payment to eligible and identifiable investors and making a claim to the Fund. Therefore, unclaimed amounts can still be claimed by the unitholders to the REIT, which then seeks a refund from the Board for the said amount.

rows.query: When a listed company evaluates its board chairperson, what extra qualities are they supposed to be assessed on beyond regular director criteria?
rows.answer_text:
When a listed company evaluates its board chairperson, they are supposed to be assessed on additional qualities beyond the regular director criteria. These include:

- **Independence**: The person should be independent from the entity and other directors, with no conflict of interest.
- **Independent views and judgement**: The person should exercise their own judgment and voice opinions freely.
- **Effectiveness of leadership and ability to steer meetings**: The person should display efficient leadership, be open-minded, decisive, courteous, and able to coordinate discussions.
- **Impartiality**: The Chairperson should be impartial in conducting discussions, seeking views, and dealing with dissent.
- **Commitment**: The Chairperson should be sufficiently committed to the Board and its meetings.
- **Ability to keep shareholders' interests in mind**: The Chairperson should be able to keep shareholders' interests in mind during discussions and decisions.

These additional qualities are crucial for the Chairperson's role in ensuring the board's effectiveness and integrity.

rows.query: If most of the money in an AIF scheme comes from investors based in a country that shares a land border with India, is extra background-checking required before investing?
rows.answer_text: Yes, extra background-checking is required before investing in an AIF scheme where the corpus of the scheme is contributed by investors from a country that shares a land border with India. This is specified in the circular under the section "8.2.1. For every scheme of AIFs where 50 percent or more of the corpus of the scheme is contributed by investors – (a) who are citizens of/are from/are situated in a country which shares land border with India, or (b) whose beneficial owners, as determined in terms of sub-rule (3) of Rule 9 of the Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, are citizens of/are from/are situated in a country which shares land border with India." The necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA shall be carried out prior to making any investment.

rows.query: How often does a KYC Registration Agency need to run a penetration test on its systems, and does that change if its systems are classified as sensitive infrastructure?
rows.answer_text: A KYC Registration Agency (KRA) needs to conduct a periodic vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT) on its systems at least once in a financial year. If the systems are identified as "protected system" by NCIIPC under the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000, the VAPT shall be conducted at least twice in a financial year. Additionally, all KRAs are required to engage only CERT-In empaneled organizations for conducting VAPT. The final report on said VAPT shall be submitted to SEBI after approval from the Technology Committee of respective KRAs, within one month of completion of VAPT activity.

rows.query: If my portfolio manager changes the fees they charge, does that count as a 'material change' they need to formally disclose?
rows.answer_text: Yes, if your portfolio manager changes the fees they charge, they need to formally disclose this as a 'material change' under the PM Regulation. This is specified in the Circular for Portfolio Managers, which states that a 'material change' shall include "change in fees charged, charges associated with the services offered, investment approaches offered (along with the impact of such change) and such other changes as specified by SEBI from time to time."

rows.query: If an investment adviser outsources some work to a firm in another country, does the outsourcing contract need to spell out which country's laws apply if there's a dispute?
rows.answer_text: Yes, the outsourcing contract should include choice-of-law provisions and agreement covenants that provide for adjudication of disputes under the laws of a specific jurisdiction to address potential obstacles in exercising oversight and management of the arrangements when the intermediary outsources its activities to a foreign third party. This ensures that disputes are resolved according to the laws of the country where the dispute arises, providing a fair and consistent resolution process.

rows.query: Do asset management companies need a dedicated technology committee, and does it have to include an outside tech expert?
rows.answer_text: Yes, asset management companies (AMCs) need a dedicated technology committee, and it is advised to include an independent external expert with adequate experience in the area of technology in the Mutual Fund industry / BFSI. This committee should review the cyber security and cyber resilience framework for Mutual Funds / AMCs, as well as the system audit related aspects of AMCs. The committee should be chaired by an expert in technology and should include at least one independent external expert with adequate experience in the area of technology in Mutual Fund industry / BFSI.

rows.query: Why do mutual fund schemes benchmark their performance against a 'total return index' instead of a plain price index?
rows.answer_text:
Mutual fund schemes benchmark their performance against a 'total return index' instead of a plain price index for the following reasons:

1. **Incorporation of Dividends and Interest Payments**: Total Return Index (TRI) takes into account all dividends, interest payments, and capital gains, which are generated from the basket of constituents that make up the index. This makes the TRI more comprehensive and reflective of the actual returns of the scheme.

2. **Comparison to Benchmark**: By benchmarking against the TRI, mutual fund schemes can compare their performance more accurately to the index, which is a widely recognized benchmark in the market.

3. **Inclusion of All Returns**: The TRI includes all returns, including dividends, interest payments, and capital gains, which are crucial for assessing the true performance of the scheme.

4. **Performance Comparison**: Using the TRI as a benchmark allows mutual fund schemes to compare their performance against the broader market, providing a more comprehensive view of their performance.

rows.query: What kinds of risk limits does a broker have to apply to a client's direct market access orders?
rows.answer_text:
A broker has to apply the following risk limits to a client's direct market access orders:

1. Order quantity/order value limit in terms of price and quantity specified for the client.
2. All position limits specified in the derivatives segment as applicable.
3. Net position that can be outstanding so as to fully cover the risk emanating from the trades with the available margins of the specific client.
4. Appropriate limits for securities which are subject to FII limits as specified by the Reserve Bank of India.

rows.query: If shares held in demat form are pledged as loan collateral and the account holder dies, can the nominee get those shares transferred before the loan is cleared?
rows.answer_text: Yes, the nominee can get those shares transferred before the loan is cleared. According to the Circular ID #90, if shares held in demat form are pledged as loan collateral and the account holder dies, the AMC or DP will transmit the folio / account to the nominee(s) upon receipt of 1) copy of the death certificate and 2) completion/updation of KYC of the nominee(s). The nominee is not required to provide affidavits, indemnitites, undertakings, attestations or notarization. The AMC / DP will not consider the power of attorney as equivalent to the collection of margin by the TM / CM in respect of securities held in the demat account of the client.

rows.query: If my stockbroker's trading system goes down, is there a backup platform that lets me still close out my open positions?
rows.answer_text: Yes, if your stockbroker's trading system goes down, there is a backup platform that allows you to still close out your open positions. This is facilitated by the Stock Exchanges providing an alternative contingency trading framework, specifically the Contingency Pool Trading facility. This facility operates via the exchange's internal network within its physical premises, where broker allocated dedicated terminals are seamlessly connected to the Stock Exchange trading platform. Additionally, Stock Exchanges are advised to ensure the availability of an alternative mode of trading system in case of failure of the Smart Order Routing facility.

rows.query: What percentage of distribution may an InvIT retain under Regulation 18(6), computed jointly at SPV and Trust level?
rows.answer_text: The InvIT may retain **10%** of the distribution under Regulation 18(6), computed jointly at SPV and Trust levels. This is based on the illustration provided in the circular, where the combined NDCF for computing Max retention is calculated by adding the NDCF of SPV's (B) to the NDCF of Trust's (A) and then subtracting the amount distributed by SPV's (C). The maximum retention amount is then calculated as 10% of the difference between the combined NDCF and the distributed amount.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for depositories, are depository participants required to send quarterly statements of transactions to clients whose demat accounts have no transactions and no security balances?
rows.answer_text: Yes, under the current master circular for depositories, depository participants are required to send quarterly statements of transactions to clients whose demat accounts have no transactions and no security balances. However, they are exempt from sending these statements if the client is informed in advance that they will not receive such statements until there are any transactions or security holdings in the demat account.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for depositories, for what two purposes can a client's Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) be utilized by a stock broker or stock broker depository participant?
rows.answer_text:
Under the current master circular for depositories, a client's Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) can be utilized by a stock broker or stock broker depository participant for the following two purposes:

1. To access the Beneficial Owner (BO) account of the client to meet the settlement obligations of the trade executed by the client on the Stock Exchange through the same stock broker.

2. To pledge or re-pledge securities in favor of the TM/CM for the purpose of meeting the margin requirements of the clients in connection with the trades executed by the clients on the Stock Exchange.

rows.answer_text:
Under the current master circular for Alternative Investment Funds, an AIF scheme is not required to maintain investors' pro-rata rights in a particular investment under the following circumstances:

- An investor has been excused or excluded from participating in the investment.
- An investor has defaulted on providing their pro-rata contribution for the investment.

rows.query: Per SEBI's November 2022 circular on declaration of First Close for AIFs, what one-time transitional deadline applied to existing AIF schemes that had not yet declared their First Close as of the date of that circular, and does the AIF Master Circular (issued June 03, 2026, last updated June 16, 2026) still carry this transitional deadline for pre-existing schemes?

- The AIF Master Circular (issued June 3, 2026, last updated June 16, 2026) still carries this transitional deadline for pre-existing schemes.

- The circular explicitly states that the updated Master Circular for AIFs is available on the SEBI website at the specified path.

- The circular also mentions that the updated Master Circular for AIFs has been updated with the provisions of this circular.

- The circular provides specific details on the timeline for declaration of First Close, including the date of the circular itself.

- The circular specifies that the First Close of the scheme shall be declared by an AIF in the manner as may be specified by SEBI from time to time.

rows.query: Under which regulation is the Base Minimum Capital Deposit requirement for Category 2 Execution Only Platforms prescribed, and is that regulatory basis still current?
rows.answer_text:
The Base Minimum Capital Deposit requirement for Category 2 Execution Only Platforms is prescribed under the Circular SEBI/HO/MRD/POD-III/CIR/2023/165, which was issued on October 6, 2023. This circular realigns the BMC requirements with the risk profiles of stock brokers/trading members in the cash/derivative segment of the stock exchange. The current regulatory basis for this requirement is the Circular SEBI/HO/CDMRD/DMP/P/CIR/2022/64 dated March 21, 2022, which provides the BMC requirements for Trading Members.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) that are no longer in force — SEBI/HO/CDMRD/DMP/P/CIR/2022/64 has been superseded by SEBI/HO/MRD/MRD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/136. Refer to the superseding circular(s) for current requirements.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) resting on a repealed regulation — SEBI/HO/MRD/POD-III/CIR/2023/165 rests on the Stock Brokers Regulations, 1992, which has been repealed and replaced by the Stock Brokers Regulations, 2026. Refer to the current regulation(s) for the governing requirements.

rows.query: What documents make up the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) that stock brokers must give clients free of charge, and is the stock-broker regulation underpinning this MITC requirement still current?
rows.answer_text:
The documents that make up the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) that stock brokers must give clients free of charge include:

1. Account opening form
2. Rights and obligations
3. Risk disclosure documents
4. Guidance note
5. Policies and procedures
6. Tariff sheet

The stock-broker regulation underpinning this MITC requirement is still current as of the latest circular dated January 08, 2025, which specifies the minimum mandatory terms and conditions to be disclosed by Research Analysts (RAs) under Regulation 24(6) of the SEBI (Research Analysts) Regulations, 2014. This regulation also specifies that the terms and conditions shall include the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) to be disclosed by RAs, which are to be standardized by Industry Standards Forum (ISF) in consultation with RAASB and SEBI.

rows.query: Which prior Master Circular did the April 2013 Master Circular for Depositories supersede, and is the depositories regulation it was issued under still in force?
rows.answer_text:
The April 2013 Master Circular for Depositories superseded the previous Master Circular CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 dated April 15, 2013. The depositories regulation it was issued under, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (Issue and Listing of Debt Securities) Regulations, 2008, is still in force.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) that are no longer in force — CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 has been superseded by CIR/MRD/DP/11/2014, SEBI/HO/MRD/DP/CIR/P/2016/134. Refer to the superseding circular(s) for current requirements.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) resting on a repealed regulation — CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 rests on the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 1996, which has been repealed and replaced by the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 2018; CIR/MRD/DP/11/2014 rests on the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 1996, which has been repealed and replaced by the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 2018. Refer to the current regulation(s) for the governing requirements.

rows.query: Whose bank account may be used for payment of a Mutual Fund investment made in the name of a minor through a guardian, and is the Mutual Funds regulation underpinning this rule still in force?
rows.answer_text:
The rule underpinning the payment of a Mutual Fund investment made in the name of a minor through a guardian is outlined in the Master Circular for Mutual Funds, specifically in Section 15.13.2. This section states that all redemption proceeds shall be credited only in the verified bank account of the minor, i.e., the account the minor may hold with the parent/legal guardian after completing all KYC formalities.

The regulation is still in force as evidenced by the Master Circular for Mutual Funds, which is part of the ongoing regulatory framework for the Mutual Fund industry. This circular provides guidelines for the process of investments made in the name of a minor through a guardian, ensuring that the minor's account is the primary vehicle for receiving investment proceeds.
